spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: A single complex phase-space function is designed so that different projections recover three objects: the real h-marginal is eigenvalue density, the imaginary h-marginal is potential derivative, and the theta-marginal is Young density. directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The text defines complex Omega(h,theta) with h-integral 2R(e^{i theta})-1. Its real and imaginary parts integrate over h to rho(theta) and V'(theta), respectively, while theta integration cancels the odd imaginary contribution and yields u(h). The real part is a constant-density indicator between h_-(theta) and h_+(theta); the imaginary part is expressed through Heaviside regions determined by the beta_n sine series.
directed.conceptual_reading: The construction packages complementary marginals without claiming they are identical. It distinguishes state-dependent geometry from model-fixed forcing by assigning them to real and imaginary components.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Omega, the resolvent boundary value, constant-density droplet indicators, and marginalization link eigenvalues, potential, and Young diagrams.

Integrating over theta gives inverse branches x(J-tilde)^{-1}; because J-tilde is not one-to-one, infinitely many branches appear, in analogy with the Young distribution.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Mellin transformation turns approximation by fractional-part kernels into multiplication by zeta, so density in a function space becomes a zero-exclusion statement. Discrete dilations strengthen the criterion, while the more general kernel route exposes compact support as the obstruction to using analytic kernels in the converse.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The Mellin transform of rho_theta(t)={theta/t} is -theta^s zeta(s)/s in the critical strip. Nyman-Beurling states RH equivalently as L2 approximation of the indicator by such functions with theta in (0,1], and Baez-Duarte restricts to theta=1/n. A general strong criterion uses Muntz transforms of good kernels; RH gives approximation, while the stated converse assumes compact support and a zero-free Mellin transform.
directed.conceptual_reading: Approximation error is converted into analytic information because a hypothetical zero annihilates the kernel transforms but not the target transform. Restricting the dictionary and broadening the target kernel reveal different proof burdens.

Jensen gives only pNB implies gNB, so they support different extraction and tail arguments.

The inequality between square of expectation and expectation of square gives D-bar_n^2 at most D_n^2. The roadmap associates pNB with positive-probability extraction and concentration near 1/k, while gNB requires moment and coefficient-tail control for noncompact variables.
directed.conceptual_reading: Moving expectation across a nonlinear squared norm changes the information retained. pNB controls samplewise performance strongly enough to seek a deterministic realization; gNB controls only the averaged representation and needs separate anti-tail conditions.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Small expected random error is converted into one deterministic Nyman-Beurling witness by intersecting two positive-probability events: good approximation and simultaneous support in (0,1]. Given pNB, Markov's inequality makes the event of L2 error at most epsilon have probability greater than 1-nu for a suitable n. Since the support event has probability greater than nu, their intersection is nonempty, and evaluating the variables at one outcome supplies a deterministic NB approximation; hence RH.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is a probabilistic-method existence proof: expectation controls the size of a bad set, while support admissibility ensures a good sample also lies in the deterministic dictionary.

On (1,infinity), the fractional parts reduce to theta_k/t and the coefficient sum is bounded by the same L2 error, so both pieces tend to zero, contradicting 1/s.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The expected fractional-part kernel of a random dilation is exactly the negative Muntz transform of its survival function. This identity converts a probabilistic object into a deterministic analytic kernel and makes existing Baez-Duarte approximation machinery available.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For positive integrable X with survival function f(x)=P(X>=x), tail integration and decomposition into unit intervals give E{X} as the integral of f minus its integer samples. Scaling X by t yields E{X/t}=-P f(t), where P is the Muntz transform. If X has a continuous density with suitable integrability, f is a good kernel and the same identity follows by integration against f'.
directed.conceptual_reading: Expectation is not merely averaging noise here; it performs a representation change from random fractional parts to a deterministic transform with known Mellin behavior.
